scenario: AITA for Refusing to Pump my GF's Tire? | Whenever my GF's car has any sort of maintenance issue she tries to hold me accountable for finding the issue, fixing it, or taking it to get fixed. When she had an issue with one of her tires a while ago I was the first to notice how low it was and gave her a heads up as she was leaving for work. A day later it was completely flat because she didn't pump air in it (or get it inspected). So I ended up doing it for her. At that time I also decided to buy her PSI gauge and showed her how to use it. This was about the extent of my capabilities and when I started to notice a pattern of other car-related demands I made it very clear that I don't know shit about fixing cars besides the very basics (changing a tire, pumping air, pouring oil, jumps starts). She still insisted that I call her Dad and ask questions or watch youtube videos to learn how. My response was that I'd prefer that a mechanic take care of it and that she could learn to do these things if she wanted. ​ Now another tire has a slow leak and needs to be refilled about once a week or two (not entirely sure bc I've never seen it completely flat). She insists that I check the pressure every morning before work and drive it to the gas station to fill the tire as needed (until she gets it fixed/replaced). She says she never noticed the leak before and had to rely on the help of strangers to check the pressure and pump the tire for her. ​ I asked why she needed strangers (they're always men btw) to do something that I've taught her how to do already. She claimed that she didn't know how, didn't want to get dirty, and ultimately its a man's responsibility. I told her that as a car owner (man or woman) you should know how do something as basic as pump a tire and change a flat (especially since I showed her how). I told her that it seemed like she was playing the "Damsel in distress" role and acting completely helpless on purpose. I also reminded her that she could be stranded one day and may need to know how to do these things instead of relying on the generosity of complete strangers. She replied saying that all of her male friends/family agreed with her and that they were "real men" b/c they knew how to take care of a woman. ​ I don't really care for the silly, outdated gender role bs and I've made it very clear. On top of that I do plenty of handy work around the house, cook and clean regularly ( I cook more often than she does in fact), and I pay majority of our expenses (including all of the rent). The way I see it, this shouldn't make me any less of a man in her eyes. I also never hold her to lofty standards, or stereotypical expectations just bc she's a woman, but she always seems comfortable doing it to me. ​ To settle the issue, I offered again to show her how to use the pump while we were at the gas station this past weekend. She flatly refused..... So now I'm determined not to lift a finger. AITA here?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being unreasonable in this situation with my girlfriend. Let me start by laying out what's been happening. Whenever her car has any maintenance issues, she expects me to handle it—whether that's fixing it myself, taking it to a mechanic, or just figuring out what's wrong. I mean, I get that she might not know much about cars, but I'm not exactly a car expert either. I can do some basic stuff like changing a tire, pumping air, pouring oil, and jump-starting the car, but that's about it. A while back, she had a tire that was low on air. I noticed it and told her about it before she left for work. But instead of taking care of it herself or getting it checked out, she just ignored it, and a day later, the tire was completely flat. So, I ended up having to fix it for her. To help her out, I even bought her a PSI gauge and showed her how to use it. I thought that would solve the problem, but it seems like it's just the beginning. Now, another tire has a slow leak and needs to be refilled about once a week or two. She insists that I check the pressure every morning before work and drive her to the gas station to fill the tire as needed until she gets it fixed or replaced. She claims she never noticed the leak before and had to rely on strangers to help her check the pressure and pump the tire. I asked her why she needed strangers to do something I've already taught her how to do, and she said she didn't know how, didn't want to get dirty, and ultimately, it's a man's responsibility. I told her that as a car owner, whether male or female, you should know how to do something as basic as pumping a tire and changing a flat, especially since I've already shown her how. I mentioned that it seemed like she was playing the "Damsel in Distress" role and acting completely helpless on purpose. I also reminded her that she could be stranded one day and might need to know how to do these things instead of relying on strangers. She replied that all her male friends and family agreed with her and that they were "real men" because they knew how to take care of a woman. I don't really care for these outdated gender roles, and I've made that clear. Plus, I do plenty of handywork around the house, cook and clean regularly, and pay the majority of our expenses, including all the rent. I don't see how that makes me any less of a man in her eyes. I also don't hold her to any stereotypical expectations just because she's a woman, but she seems comfortable doing it to me. To try to settle the issue, I offered again to show her how to use the pump while we were at the gas station this past weekend, but she flatly refused. Now, I'm determined not to lift a finger. Am I being unreasonable here? Is it fair for me to refuse to help her with something I've already taught her how to do, especially when she's relying on strangers for help? I guess part of me feels like I've already done my part by teaching her and providing the tools she needs. It's frustrating when she doesn't take the initiative to learn or do things herself, especially when it comes to something as basic as maintaining her car. I also don't appreciate the gender role expectations she's imposing on me, especially since I contribute a lot to our relationship in other ways. On the other hand, I can understand that she might feel overwhelmed or uncomfortable with car maintenance, and maybe she's not as confident in her abilities as I am. But I've already given her the resources and shown her how to do it, so it's hard to see why she's still relying on others or expecting me to handle it for her. I also wonder if there's a deeper issue here about communication and expectations in our relationship. Maybe we need to have a more open and honest conversation about our roles and responsibilities, not just regarding car maintenance but in general. It's possible that she has certain expectations that I'm not fully aware of, or that I'm not communicating my feelings clearly. Overall, I'm torn between wanting to support her and feeling like I'm being taken advantage of or held to unreasonable standards because of outdated gender roles. I need to find a balance where I can respect her needs while also asserting my own boundaries and expectations for our relationship.
